title: URL intelligence upgrade evaluation (url_rules_v3 + url_fusion_v3 + host-only model input)
method_notes: Untouched PhiUSIIL test split (36,901 URLs); nothing fitted or tuned on it.

Legitimate-with-path robustness slice: 2,000 legitimate test hosts with one of eight ordinary paths appended (seed 20261106). The original legitimate rows are all bare homepages, so they cannot reveal path-based false alarms.
No URL was requested or opened; all checks are offline string analysis.
honest_reading: Phishing URLs reaching Elevated or High rose from 0.2% to 51.9%; High from 0% to 2.3% (brand impersonation, look-alike, free hosting, risky endings).
Legitimate links with ordinary paths: warned 22.1% (was 100%), Elevated or High 0.1%. Paths with account words such as /login keep a Caution by design.

Policy choice made with these measurements: without the rule 'weak evidence on a strongly phishing-like host is Elevated', phishing at Elevated or above was 3.0% instead of the figure above, with the same legitimate-with-path false-alarm rate within 0.1 points. Known false alarm: a popular site the host model misjudges (for example github.com/login) can reach Elevated.
PhiUSIIL phishing URLs are mostly not Malaysian-brand impersonations; the brand list mainly helps on local lures, which this dataset under-represents.
